name: PDF to PDF/A
description: Create a picture-based PDF/A-2b copy for archiving.

help.summary: Save each visible page as a picture in a PDF/A-2b archive copy. This is useful when a fixed page appearance matters; it removes selectable text and interactive features. Check the receiving archive’s requirements first.
steps: Choose a PDF and the picture quality.
Read Good to know. Pages become pictures, so keep your original.
Select Create PDF/A, then check the preview and small print.
Download the copy. Validate it for your archive’s requirements and keep the original.
options: Picture quality
200 DPI or 300 DPI. Higher resolution keeps finer print and creates larger files. Large pages use a lower resolution to fit memory.
Good to know and More
Text, links and comments become pictures; bookmarks, attachments and saved details are not copied.

limits.inputs: Standard PDFs without switchable layers or XFA. Flatten fillable pages first. Unlock opening-password files first.
limits.size: 128 MB input/output/picture working set. Each rendered page is bounded to 12 megapixels and 8,192 pixels per side.
limits.pages: All pages, up to 100 per PDF. A two-minute deadline and Cancel protect the browser.
limits.browsers: Current browsers with local workers. Colour profile and tool assets are included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: Each PDF uses the same resolution and picture acknowledgement independently.

name: Grayscale PDF
description: Convert colour pictures or whole pages to shades of grey.

help.summary: Choose Pictures only to keep text, shapes, links and forms unchanged, or Entire page to convert everything visible to grey. Preview the new copy before downloading.
steps: Choose a PDF with the colours you want to convert.
Choose Pictures only or Entire page. For whole pages, choose a page range and resolution.
Click Convert to grayscale.
Compare the original and result, then download your new copy.
options: Pictures only
Converts separate embedded colour pictures at their original dimensions across all pages. Text and shapes retain their colours. Inline pictures need Entire page.
Entire page
Selected pages become grey pictures. Text is no longer selectable, links and comments lose interactivity on those pages, and accessibility tags are removed from the new copy.
Picture quality
Higher DPI creates larger, sharper whole-page pictures. Very large pages may use a lower resolution to fit browser memory.

limits.inputs: Standard PDFs without switchable layers or XFA. Whole-page conversion of fillable pages needs Flatten PDF first.
limits.size: 128 MB input/output/converted-picture working set. Each picture is limited to 12 megapixels and 8,192 pixels per side.
limits.pages: Up to 500 source pages; 100 whole pages or 200 colour pictures per run, with a two-minute deadline.
limits.browsers: Current browsers with local workers. Included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: Each file uses the same settings independently. Review the output before sharing.

name: Rasterize PDF
description: Turn PDF pages into pictures inside a new PDF.

help.summary: Rasterize PDF replaces selected pages' visible text, graphics and marks with pictures. Other pages stay unchanged. This can help with fixed page appearance; it is not compression or secure data removal.
steps: Choose a PDF and the pages to convert, or leave the range empty for all.
Choose the picture resolution.
Click Turn pages into pictures and compare the result with the original.
Download the new PDF and keep the original.
options: Pages (leave blank for all)
Convert all pages or selected ranges. Pages you leave out keep their original content.
Picture quality
72, 144, 200 or 300 DPI. Higher values create larger pictures; unusually large pages are bounded to fit memory.

limits.inputs: Standard PDFs without switchable layers or XFA. Selected fillable pages need Flatten PDF first.
limits.size: 128 MB input/output/converted-picture working set. Rendering is bounded to 12 megapixels and 8,192 pixels per side.
limits.pages: Up to 500 source pages; select up to 100 per run. A two-minute deadline and Cancel protect the browser.
limits.browsers: Current browsers with local workers. Included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: Each PDF uses the same page range and resolution independently.

name: Deskew PDF
description: Straighten slightly tilted scanned pages.

help.summary: Deskew PDF looks for a clear text tilt up to five degrees. Corrected pages become pictures with extra white edge space, so their corners are not cropped. Uncertain or already straight pages keep their original content.
steps: Choose your scanned PDF.
Choose the pages and picture resolution.
Click Straighten pages and review the reported page corrections.
Compare original and corrected pages before downloading.
options: Pages (leave blank for all)
Only selected pages are examined. A page changes only when a clear small tilt is found.
Picture quality
Higher DPI keeps small scanned text sharper but uses more memory.

limits.inputs: Standard PDFs without switchable layers or XFA. Selected fillable pages need Flatten PDF first.
limits.size: 128 MB input/output/converted-picture working set. Rendered input is bounded to 12 megapixels; expanded output to 16 megapixels and 8,192 pixels per side.
limits.pages: Up to 500 source pages; examine up to 100 per run with a two-minute deadline.
limits.browsers: Current browsers with local workers. Included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: Every file is examined independently; no tilt or recognition accuracy is guaranteed.

name: Print-friendly PDF
description: Lighten scanned paper for black-and-white printing.

help.summary: Turn selected pages into grey or black-and-white pictures, lighten paper and adjust contrast. Review faint writing and stamps carefully: cleaning can remove meaningful detail. This does not guarantee printer ink savings.
steps: Choose a PDF and, optionally, the pages to prepare.
Choose resolution, paper lightening and contrast.
Optionally choose black and white only or reduce small specks.
Click Make print-friendly and compare the result before downloading or printing.
options: Lighten paper and shadows
Removes yellow tint through grey conversion and brightens estimated paper shading.
Contrast
Makes dark and light areas more or less distinct.
Black and white only
Replaces grey with black or white. Adjust the cutoff to keep the writing you need.
Reduce small specks
Removes isolated tiny marks. It may also remove punctuation or faint details; compare carefully.

limits.inputs: Standard PDFs without switchable layers or XFA. Selected fillable pages need Flatten PDF first.
limits.size: 128 MB input/output/converted-picture working set. Rendering is bounded to 12 megapixels and 8,192 pixels per side.
limits.pages: Up to 500 source pages; prepare up to 100 per run, with a two-minute deadline.
limits.browsers: Current browsers with local workers. Included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: Each PDF uses the same settings independently. Always review light writing and stamps.

name: Headers & Footers
description: Add page numbers, dates and text above and below your pages.

help.summary: Add text above and below your PDF pages. Choose each section separately and use page numbers, the filename, today’s date or your own variables. Existing page text and pictures stay in place.
steps: Choose a PDF.
Enter text in Header centre or Footer centre. Open More options for left and right positions.
Use the insertion buttons for page numbers, file names or dates. Check the live preview, then select Add headers & footers.
Check Preview result and download your PDF. For several PDFs, use Process all files.
options: Header and Footer
Centre fields are shown first; left and right fields are in More options. If the text does not fit, shorten it or choose a smaller size.
Insert page number, total pages, file name or date
Click a text box, then use an insertion button. Its label is filled in with the original page number, total pages, file name or today’s date when you save. Typed placeholders still work.
Custom variables
Write name=value, one per line, then use {name} in your text. Unknown or repeated names are reported.
Pages (leave blank for all)
Leave empty for all pages or enter a range such as 1–3, 5. Page numbers refer to the original document, even when only some pages are selected.
Margin (mm)
Distance from the visible page edges in millimetres. Preview the result to avoid covering existing content.

limits.inputs: Standard PDFs. Switchable layers and XFA forms need a fixed standard copy first.
limits.size: Up to 128 MB input and output; available browser memory may require less.
limits.pages: Up to 500 pages, with a two-minute deadline. Each text section is one line, up to 1,000 characters, and must fit the visible margins.
limits.browsers: Current browsers with local workers. This tool is included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: The shared queue processes files independently; failed files do not remove successful results.

name: Resize PDF Pages
description: Change paper size and fit your pages with optional margins.

help.summary: Change the paper size of all or selected pages. Fit keeps the whole page inside your margins, Fill trims visible edges, and Stretch changes width and height separately. Text remains selectable and image data is not recompressed.
steps: Choose a PDF and, if needed, enter the pages to resize.
Select a paper size or enter a custom width and height in millimetres.
Choose Fit, Fill or Stretch, orientation and margins, then select Resize PDF.
Use Preview result to compare your pages before downloading.
options: Paper size
A3, A4, A5, Letter, Legal or custom dimensions. Orientation uses the short and long sides for portrait or landscape.
Fit
Keeps proportions and includes the whole visible page. Spare space becomes white margins.
Fill
Keeps proportions and fills the space inside your margins. Overflow is hidden, not securely deleted.
Stretch
Matches the available width and height independently. Letters and pictures can change shape.
Pages (leave blank for all)
Only selected pages change size. Other pages keep their original boxes, rotation and content.

limits.inputs: Standard PDFs. XFA or switchable layers need a fixed copy; unsupported interactive appearances need Flatten PDF first.
limits.size: Up to 128 MB input and output, with physical page dimensions up to 200 inches per side.
limits.pages: Up to 500 pages, with a two-minute deadline. Optional ranges preserve all unselected pages.
limits.browsers: Current browsers with local workers. This tool is included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: Each PDF uses the same settings independently. Review results when source pages have different sizes.

name: Fast Web View
description: Prepare PDFs to open sooner in compatible online viewers.

help.summary: Prepare a PDF for progressive loading in viewers that support Fast Web View. The local QPDF engine rearranges the file and verifies its page-loading hints. It does not downsample pictures or replace text, and the output may be larger. Viewing speed also depends on the viewer and hosting server.
steps: Choose a PDF and click Apply Fast Web View.
If the document has a digital signature, read the warning and acknowledge that a new copy invalidates it. Keep the original.
Wait for Fast Web View verified, then use Preview result to check the generated PDF.
Download PDF. For several documents, use Process all files and download the successful results separately or together.
options: Apply Fast Web View
Rewrites the file for progressive loading without changing image resolution or text. A verification failure prevents download.
Preview result
Shows the actual generated PDF. Original and Side by side views are available for unencrypted documents.
Digital signatures
A rewritten copy invalidates existing cryptographic signatures. The original file remains unchanged. Signed batch files fail individually unless you have acknowledged this for the selected files.
Process all files
Prepares each PDF independently. If a file fails or is password-locked, the other successful results remain available.
Cancel
Stops the document and engine workers. Cancelled jobs cannot return a result after cancellation.

limits.inputs: PDF files, including owner-restricted files that open with an empty password. PDFs requiring an opening password need an unlocked copy first.
limits.size: Up to 128 MB input and output. File restructuring can increase size; browser memory may require a smaller file.
limits.pages: Up to 2,000 pages, with a two-minute processing deadline. Actual loading speed depends on the viewer and host.
limits.browsers: A current browser with workers, cryptographic hashing and gzip decompression. The local engine is included in the initial offline cache.
limits.batch: Up to 100 files within the shared queue's memory budget. Each PDF is prepared and checked separately; failed files are reported.

name: Extract Images
description: Save embedded pictures as separate image files.

help.summary: Save pictures stored inside your PDF. Ordinary JPG images keep their original bytes. Other supported pictures become PNG files at their embedded resolution. This does not take a screenshot of the page or turn drawings into pictures.
steps: Choose a PDF with embedded pictures and select Extract images.
Review the available pictures and any notice about images that could not be read separately.
Use Minimum width, Minimum height or Minimum file size to leave out smaller pictures. Zero keeps all available images.
Choose Preview image, then Download image. Create image ZIP saves all matching images together; add several PDFs to use the batch queue.
options: Preview image
See one matching picture at a time. The page list shows where its image resource is stored; shared pictures appear once.
Minimum width (pixels) and Minimum height (pixels)
Width and height refer to the embedded pixels, not the size of the picture on a printed PDF page. A small logo can have fewer pixels than a page scan.
Minimum file size (KB)
Filters the extracted image file size. PNG size can differ from the compressed image stream stored inside the PDF.
Create image ZIP
Includes every available image matching your filters. Changing a filter clears the old ZIP. Original JPG bytes are preserved when the PDF does not override their colour or transparency.
Process all files
Creates one image ZIP per PDF. A file with extraction notices is reported for individual review rather than silently delivering an incomplete archive.

limits.inputs: PDFs with embedded page or Form image resources. Opening-password documents need an unlocked copy first; empty-password owner restrictions are authenticated locally.
limits.size: Up to 128 MB input and 128 MB combined extracted output. Each image is limited to 12 million pixels and an 8,192-pixel edge.
limits.pages: Up to 2,000 pages and 200 separate images. Finding nested image resources and decoding images are subject to time limits; your device may need a smaller document.
limits.browsers: Use a current browser with local PDF workers and PNG canvas encoding. Physical-device memory capacity varies.
limits.batch: The shared batch queue accepts up to 100 PDFs within its combined memory limit. Review files with partial-extraction notices individually.

name: PDF Reader
description: Read, search and copy text from your PDF.

help.summary: Read a PDF, search for words and copy selectable text. Jump to a page or bookmark, adjust the view and download the unchanged original.
steps: Choose a PDF to read.
Use Page, Previous or Next to move through the document. Open Pages and bookmarks for thumbnails and headings.
Change Zoom to read comfortably. Open Find in document to search, or More options to change the view.
Open More options to Download original or Print.
options: Find text
Open Find in document to search selectable text. Enter finds the next match; Shift+Enter finds the previous one. Scanned words need OCR first.
Page view
Open More options. Continuous shows scrolling pages; Single page shows one page at a time.
Rotate view
Turn the view without changing the original PDF.
Fullscreen and Presentation
Use the whole screen when your browser supports it. Presentation switches to a fitted single page; focus PDF pages to use arrow or Page Up/Down keys. Escape exits fullscreen.
Print
Open the unchanged original in your browser's PDF view and use its Print command. If the tab is blocked, download and print in your usual reader.

limits.inputs: PDF files that open without a password. Use Unlock PDF first when an opening password is required.
limits.size: Up to 128 MB. Page previews limit resolution to reduce memory use; your device may need a smaller file.
limits.pages: Up to 2,000 pages and 2,000 bookmark entries. Thumbnails show nearby pages; the Page control can navigate throughout the document.
limits.browsers: Use a current browser. Fullscreen depends on browser support; native printing opens the original in a separate browser PDF view.
limits.batch: One PDF is displayed at a time. Choosing another clears the previous document from this workspace.

name: RTF to PDF
description: Turn rich-text paragraphs into a readable PDF.

help.summary: Open a rich-text document and turn its text into a readable PDF. Paragraphs, bold, italic and strikethrough are kept. Choose a fresh page layout, check the preview and download a new copy.
steps: Select Open RTF file and choose your .rtf document.
Check the Live preview and any messages about formatting or pictures.
Choose the paper size, orientation, text size, line spacing and margins.
Select Create PDF, check every page and select Download PDF.
options: Live preview
Shows the supported text and emphasis. It is a formatting preview; check page breaks in the created PDF.
Paper size and orientation
Choose A4, Letter or A3, in portrait or landscape.
Text size and line spacing
Choose 8–36 points with compact, comfortable or double spacing. The original fonts and text sizes are replaced.
Margins (mm)
Choose 5–50 mm of space around the text.
Process all files
Create one PDF per selected RTF with the current layout. Failed files are reported separately. Download individual copies or a ZIP.
Clear file
Remove the input and result. Browser refresh also clears working files.

limits.inputs: RTF 1 documents with text and basic emphasis. Legacy code-page bytes and RTF Unicode escapes are read by RTF.js. Output fonts cover Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text; unsupported characters are reported.
limits.size: Up to 50 KB per file and 50,000 RTF source characters after legacy-byte escaping. Use a smaller section for larger documents.
limits.pages: Up to 500 output pages in the shared builder. Complex RTF layouts and nesting are rejected. These are enforced bounds, not a completion guarantee on every device.
limits.browsers: Use a current browser. Measured results for different browsers are recorded separately. Formatting accuracy is not guaranteed for every document.
limits.batch: Up to 100 selected files and 512 MB combined, subject to the per-file limits. One failed file does not stop the others.

name: CSV to PDF
description: Turn comma-separated data into a readable PDF table.

help.summary: Create a PDF table from comma-separated data. Preview the rows, choose a paper layout and download a new copy. Leading zeros, decimal values and quoted text stay as written. Formulas are printed as text; they are never calculated.
steps: Select Open CSV file or paste comma-separated data into CSV.
Check the Live preview, especially columns, quotes and important values.
Choose your paper size, orientation, text size, line spacing and margins. Leave First row is a heading on when the first row contains column names; turn it off when every row is data.
Select Create PDF, review its pages and select Download PDF.
options: First row is a heading
On by default. The first row is bold and repeats on later table pages. Turn it off when every row contains data.
File name
Choose the name for the downloaded PDF; the CSV original stays unchanged.
Paper size
Choose A4, Letter or A3. Wider paper can help tables with more columns.
Orientation
Choose portrait or landscape. Landscape gives wide tables more room.
Text size
Choose 8–36 points. Smaller text can help long values fit; always check readability.
Line spacing
Choose spacing for multiline cells. Rows stay together where they fit; a row too tall for a page is reported.
Margins (mm)
Choose 5–50 mm of space around the table.
Process all files
Create a separate PDF for each selected CSV with the same settings. Failures are reported separately; download individual copies or a ZIP.
Clear text
Remove the current input and PDF from this workspace. Refresh also clears working files.

limits.inputs: Comma-separated CSV in UTF-8 or BOM-marked UTF-16, or pasted CSV. Quoted commas, doubled quotes and multiline fields are supported. Use the same number of columns in every row.
limits.size: Files up to 2 MB can be read; the table input is limited to 50,000 characters. Very wide values or a row taller than the page need smaller text, wider paper or a smaller section.
limits.pages: Up to 1,000 rows and 12 columns. The shared table builder has a 500-page output limit. These are enforced bounds, not a guarantee for every device.
limits.browsers: Use a current browser. Results from browser tests are recorded separately and do not guarantee that every file will finish.
limits.batch: Up to 100 selected files and 512 MB combined, subject to the per-file limits. An individual failure does not stop the other files.

name: PDF to SVG
description: Save PDF pages as SVG images, with editable text where possible.

help.summary: Create one SVG image for each selected PDF page. Simple black text can stay as editable text, with the other page content in an embedded picture. Scans and complex pages keep their complete page picture. Review the result before using it in a design.
steps: Choose your PDF. Add more than one PDF if you want to process a batch.
Choose SVG content. Editable text where possible keeps supported words as text. Page pictures keeps the entire visible page together.
Leave Pages blank for all pages, or enter a selection such as 1-3,5. Select Create SVG.
Check the preview and any notice about pages that stay as pictures. Select Download SVG files. Multiple pages arrive together in a ZIP.
options: SVG content

Editable text where possible separates simple horizontal black text from its background. Page pictures keeps everything in one image inside the SVG. Neither option turns all graphics into editable vector shapes.
Pages (leave blank for all)
Export the pages you need instead of the entire document. The SVG keeps each selected page’s own shape and orientation; pages are not stretched to match one another.
Preview page
After conversion, choose an exported page to inspect its layout. Fonts in editable text can differ from the PDF. Review important words and numbers before sharing.
Process all files
Run the same page selection and content option on each chosen PDF. A file that cannot be opened is reported separately, while the other files can finish. Download individual results or a batch ZIP.

limits.inputs: Readable PDF documents. If a password is needed to open the document, use Unlock PDF first. SVG files contain embedded pictures, not fully editable drawings.
limits.size: Inputs must be smaller than 256 MB. Generated picture data and SVG output are each limited to 128 MB. Large pictures are rendered at up to 200 DPI, with a 12-million-pixel and 4096-pixel side limit per page. These bounds control browser memory; they do not guarantee a large file will finish on every device.
limits.pages: Choose up to 200 pages per conversion. Supported editable text is limited to two million characters per conversion and 10,000 fragments per page. Choose fewer pages when a document exceeds these bounds.
limits.browsers: Generated text, rotated pages, saved forms, scans, batches, cancellation and offline conversion were checked in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit on a Mac. These checks do not guarantee results for every document. Check the output in Safari and your design application on your own device.
limits.batch: A batch accepts up to 100 input files and 512 MB total, subject to each converter’s limits. Each multi-page document produces a ZIP of its SVG pages. A batch ZIP can therefore contain smaller ZIP files.

name: Annotate PDF
description: Add text, highlights, notes and drawings to PDF pages.

help.summary: Add text, pictures, notes and drawings to a PDF. Move and style your additions, then check the saved preview. Your original stays unchanged.
steps: Choose a PDF to mark up and select its page.
Choose a common mark or open More marks. Enter any text, then drag over the page or use Add at centre.
New text boxes are selected for you. Drag the square handles to resize; text wraps automatically. Use Fit text or Width and Height for more control. Undo and Redo restore changes.
Save your annotated copy. Choose Make new marks permanent only if you do not need to edit them later.
options: Common marks and More marks
Choose a text box, highlight, drawing, rectangle or note. Open More marks for other shapes and pictures.
Page
Switch between pages; marks stay on their original pages.
Fit text, Width and Height

Drag the square handles around a selected text box to resize it. Text wraps and the box keeps enough room for your words. Fit text and Width or Height controls are also available. If the page has no room, move the box or lower Text size.
Make new marks permanent
Paint only your new marks into the page. Existing annotations and form fields are kept.
Font, Text size, Bold, Italic, Underline text, Alignment and Letter spacing
Text size stays beside your text. Open More options for font, style, alignment, spacing, visibility and rotation. Text must fit its box; check the saved preview.
Picture
Insert a PNG, JPG or WebP, then move, resize, rotate, crop or replace it. Cropping hides edges without removing the original pixels from the file.
Replace visually

After your confirmation, place a coloured cover and new text over the page. The original words remain in the file. This is not secure redaction. Use Edit PDF for supported direct text changes or Redact PDF to remove private information.
Process all files

Choose multiple files to use the settings above on each one. Results and failures appear separately. Use Cancel file, Cancel all files or Download batch as ZIP as needed. Check that page positions or form fields suit every input.

limits.inputs: PDF files that can be opened without a password. Use Unlock PDF first when necessary.
limits.size: Up to 500 new marks per copy and 2,000 characters in each text box or note. Inserted pictures are limited to 16 million pixels, an 8,192-pixel edge and 12 MB after conversion to PNG; use fewer or smaller pictures if the combined picture budget is exceeded.
limits.pages: Local tests saved a note on the last page of PDFs with 50, 300 and 1,000 simple text pages. Text boxes that would cut off text are rejected on save.
limits.browsers: All seven capacity tests passed in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including a 200 MB generated image PDF. Your file may need more memory; mobile devices and the Safari app were not tested.
limits.batch: Up to 100 input files and 512 MB total; up to 200 output files or 512 MB. ZIPs over 128 MB need Chrome/Edge direct disk saving; use individual downloads in other browsers. The Workflow stress test completed 100 synthetic files in all three engines; this does not guarantee the same capacity for every conversion.

name: Compress PDF to 50 KB
description: Try to fit a small PDF within a 50 KB form size limit.

help.summary: Choose a PDF and try to fit it within 50 KB. Some application forms accept only very small files. Text stays selectable, and a result that misses the limit is clearly marked.
steps: Choose the PDF you need under 50 KB.
Keep the 50 KB target selected, or pick another quick size.
Click Compress PDF to start working toward 50 KB. You can cancel at any time.
Check whether it reached 50 KB, compare the first page, then download your copy.
options: Target size
Starts at 50 KB. Pick a different quick size if your form allows more or less. Sizes use 1024 bytes per KB.
Remove saved document details
Optionally remove title and author properties; names printed on pages remain.
Use stronger compression
Works best with scanned PDFs and PDFs with images. Images may look blurry or lose detail. Check small print in the preview. Your target size is not guaranteed.

limits.inputs: Unlocked PDF documents, including text and images. Signed files require confirmation to create a changed copy.
limits.size: The requested size is an aim, not a guarantee. Large image files may stay above it even after compression. Stronger compression can make images noticeably softer; review the preview.
limits.pages: Tests covered 1,000 simple text pages and generated image PDFs up to 200 MB. Large files may use the full search time and remain above your target.
limits.browsers: Tested in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Large-file checks used a 100 KB target.

name: Compress PDF to 100 KB
description: Try to fit a PDF within a 100 KB upload limit.

help.summary: Choose a PDF and try to fit it within 100 KB. The search keeps selectable text and checks page appearance. A result that cannot meet the limit is clearly marked.
steps: Add the PDF you need to reduce to 100 KB.
Keep the preselected 100 KB target or enter a different size.
Click Compress PDF to start the 100 KB search. You can cancel at any time.
Check whether the 100 KB target was reached, compare the first page, and download your copy.
options: Target size
Starts at 100 KB. Select a quick size or enter a positive custom value in KB or MB. Units use 1024 bytes per KB.
Remove saved document details
Optionally remove title and author properties; names printed on pages remain.
Use stronger compression
Works best with scanned PDFs and PDFs with images. Images may look blurry or lose detail. Check small print in the preview. Your target size is not guaranteed.

limits.inputs: Unlocked PDF documents, including text and images. Signed files require confirmation to create a changed copy.
limits.size: The requested size is an aim, not a guarantee. Large image files may stay above it even after compression. Stronger compression can make images noticeably softer; review the preview.
limits.pages: Tests covered 1,000 simple text pages and generated image PDFs up to 200 MB. Large files may use the full search time and remain above your target.
limits.browsers: Tested in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Large-file checks used a 100 KB target; the other starting sizes were checked with a 50-page PDF.

name: Compress PDF to 200 KB
description: Make a PDF fit a 200 KB attachment limit when possible.

help.summary: Choose a PDF and try to fit it within 200 KB. The search keeps selectable text and checks page appearance. A result that cannot meet the limit is clearly marked.
steps: Add the PDF you need to reduce to 200 KB.
Keep the preselected 200 KB target or enter a different size.
Click Compress PDF to start the 200 KB search. You can cancel at any time.
Check whether the 200 KB target was reached, compare the first page, and download your copy.
options: Target size
Starts at 200 KB. Select a quick size or enter a positive custom value in KB or MB. Units use 1024 bytes per KB.
Remove saved document details
Optionally remove title and author properties; names printed on pages remain.
Use stronger compression

limits.size: The requested size is an aim, not a guarantee. Large image files may stay above it even after compression. Stronger compression can make images noticeably softer; review the preview.
limits.pages: Tests covered 1,000 simple text pages and generated image PDFs up to 200 MB. Large files may use the full search time and remain above your target.
limits.browsers: Tested in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Large-file checks used a 100 KB target; the other starting sizes were checked with a 50-page PDF.

name: Compress PDF to 300 KB
description: Aim for a PDF under 300 KB for online forms.

help.summary: Choose a PDF and try to fit it within 300 KB. Many online application forms set a limit around this size. Text stays selectable, and a result that misses the limit is clearly marked.
steps: Choose the PDF you need under 300 KB.
Keep the 300 KB target selected, or pick another quick size.
Click Compress PDF to start working toward 300 KB. You can cancel at any time.
Check whether it reached 300 KB, compare the first page, then download your copy.
options: Target size
Starts at 300 KB. Pick a different quick size if your form allows more or less. Sizes use 1024 bytes per KB.
Remove saved document details
Optionally remove title and author properties; names printed on pages remain.
Use stronger compression
Works best with scanned PDFs and PDFs with images. Images may look blurry or lose detail. Check small print in the preview. Your target size is not guaranteed.

limits.size: The requested size is an aim, not a guarantee. Large image files may stay above it even after compression. Stronger compression can make images noticeably softer; review the preview.
limits.pages: Tests covered 1,000 simple text pages and generated image PDFs up to 200 MB. Large files may use the full search time and remain above your target.
limits.browsers: Tested in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Large-file checks used a 100 KB target.

name: Compress PDF to 500 KB
description: Aim for a PDF smaller than 500 KB while keeping its text.

help.summary: Choose a PDF and try to fit it within 500 KB. The search keeps selectable text and checks page appearance. A result that cannot meet the limit is clearly marked.
steps: Add the PDF you need to reduce to 500 KB.
Keep the preselected 500 KB target or enter a different size.
Click Compress PDF to start the 500 KB search. You can cancel at any time.

name: Flatten PDF
description: Make filled forms, comments and stamps part of the page.

help.summary: Make supported filled forms, comments or stamps part of the printed page. Choose which categories to flatten while keeping a separate original if you need to edit them later.
steps: Choose a PDF with filled forms, comments or stamps.
Select Form fields, Comments and marks, or Signatures and stamps to choose what becomes permanent page content.
Select Flatten PDF; keep your original if you may need to edit these items later.
Select Download flattened PDF and check that the answers and marks appear correctly.
options: Form fields
Make supported filled-field appearances part of the page when the answers no longer need to be interactive.
Comments and marks
Flatten supported annotations into the page while preserving their visible appearance.
Signatures and stamps
Keep supported visible marks as page content; this does not preserve cryptographic signature validity.
Save an edited copy. Its digital signature will no longer be valid.
Shown for digitally signed input. Continue only when you want an edited copy; preserve the signed original for verification.
Process all files

Choose multiple files to use the settings above on each one. Results and failures appear separately. Use Cancel file, Cancel all files or Download batch as ZIP as needed. Check that page positions or form fields suit every input.

name: Clean PDF
description: Remove comments, attachments, scripts and saved information.

help.summary: Clean selected types of extra content from a PDF, including comments, attached files, scripts and saved information. Choose the categories you need and keep the original separately.
steps: Choose the PDF you want to clean.
Use Recommended cleanup, or open Customize cleanup to choose what to remove.
Select Clean PDF after checking that you are keeping any comments, links and form answers you still need.
Select Download cleaned PDF and review the pages and remaining document information.
options: Document details
Choose saved Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Created with, PDF software, Date created and Date modified properties to remove.
Other saved details
Remove extra properties saved by the software that created the PDF.
Hidden document details
Remove hidden descriptions saved in the PDF; camera details inside photos are not removed.
Comments and markup
Remove notes, highlights, drawings and stamps.
All comments, marks and links
Remove annotations and links while keeping fillable form fields.
Attached files and media
Remove file attachments, audio, video and 3D objects.
Automatic actions
Remove commands or links that run automatically.
Filled-in form answers
Clear current and default answers, including signature fields; also disable automatic actions.
Select all and Clear selection
Select all also includes links and filled-in answers. Clear selection lets you choose just the information you want removed.
Save an edited copy. Its digital signature will no longer be valid.
Shown for digitally signed input. Continue only when you want an edited copy; preserve the signed original for verification.
Process all files

Apply these settings to several PDFs. Each file has its own result or error. Use Cancel file or Cancel all files to stop processing, and Download batch as ZIP to save the results together. Check that page positions or form fields suit each file.

name: Compare PDFs
description: See what changed between two PDFs.

help.summary: Compare two PDFs and inspect the differences before accepting a revision or sending a final document.
steps: Choose the original as PDF A and the revision as PDF B.
Set Match pages to Automatically or By page number, then select Compare PDFs.
Read Changes summary and inspect the marked differences beside both pages.
Select Download summary to keep a text record, and manually check important differences.
options: Choose PDF A and Choose PDF B
Select the original and revised documents; both are needed for a comparison.
Match pages
Choose Automatically to try to match related pages. By page number compares pages in the same position when the order has not changed.
Matched pages
Choose a pair to inspect its visible and text differences instead of relying only on the summary.
